Remark
Source: cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0012 1. Remark after Theorem 2.1\group section-2

Under the hypotheses of Theorem 15, domination of semigroups also gives pointwise bounds for the norm of the gradient of $k_f$.

The heat kernel is obtained from Theorem 15 by taking $f_t(\lambda )=e^{-t\lambda ^2}$; its Gaussian decay is controlled by the same volume and injectivity-angle bounds.

For dimensions $2$ and $3$, the same pointwise estimates follow assuming $\Ric _M\geq (n-1)H$ and $V_{r_0}(p)\geq V>0$.

Let egin{equation} ag {2.35} \Hg =e_i e_j(g)- abla _{e_i} abla _{e_j}(g) \end{equation} denote the Hessian of $g$. The coercive estimate is egin{equation} ag {2.36} \| Hg\| _{B_{r/2}(x_0)}^{2}\le c(r)\Bigl(\| dg\| _{B_r(x_0)}^{2}+\| \Delta g\| _{B_r(x_0)}^{2}\Bigr) \end{equation} when $\Ric _M\ge H$. A lower bound for the refined injectivity angle then controls the Sobolev constant; combined with (2.36), this gives the pointwise kernel estimate in dimensions $2$ and $3$ for $f\in \mathscr {F}_1^1$.

For a $1$-form $\omega $, use the Bochner-Weitzenbock formula egin{equation} ag {2.37} (d\delta +\delta d)\omega =\sum _i igl(- abla _{e_i} abla _{e_i}+ abla _{ abla _{e_i}e_i} igr)\omega +\Ric (\omega ^*), \end{equation} where egin{equation} ag {2.38} \Ric (\omega ^*)=(\Ric (\omega ))^*, \end{equation} and $\omega ^*$ is the tangent vector dual to $\omega $. Fix a metric ball $B_r(x)$, and let $\psi (r)$ be defined by $\psi (r)|_{[0,r/2]}\equiv 1$, $\psi (r)|_{[r/2,r]}\equiv -2r/ ilde r+2$. By Stokes' theorem, egin{equation} ag {2.39} \int _{B_{ ilde r}(x_0)}\psi ^2\, d\delta dg\wedge *dg =\int _{B_{ ilde r}(x_0)}\psi ^2\delta dg\wedge *\delta dg -\int _{B_{ ilde r}(x_0)}2\psi \, d\psi \delta dg\wedge *dg. \end{equation}

Applying (2.37) to the left-hand side and integrating by parts gives \[ \int _{B_r(x_0)} \psi ^2 \delta \dg \wedge *\dg = \int _{B_r(x_0)} \left\{ \psi ^2 \sum _i \left(- abla _{e_i} abla _{e_i} + abla _{ abla _{e_i} e_i} ight)\dg \wedge *\dg + \psi ^2 \Ric (\dg ) \wedge *\dg ight\} \] egin{equation} = \int _{B_r(x_0)} \left\{ \psi ^2 \sum _i abla _{e_i}\dg \wedge * abla _{e_i}\dg + 2\psi \sum _i e_i(\psi ) abla _{e_i}\dg \wedge *\dg + \psi ^2 \Ric (\dg ) \wedge *\dg ight\} . ag {2.40} \end{equation}

If we substitute (2.40) into (2.39) and transpose the middle term we get \[ \int _{B_r(x_0)} \left( \psi ^2 \sum _i abla _{e_i}\dg \wedge * abla _{e_i}\dg + \Ric (\dg )\wedge *\dg ight) \] egin{equation} = \int _{B_r(x_0)} \psi ^2 \delta \dg \wedge *\delta \dg - \int _{B_r(x_0)} 2\psi \, d\psi \, \delta \dg \wedge *\dg - \int _{B_r(x_0)} 2\psi \sum _i e_i(\psi ) abla _{e_i}\dg \wedge *\dg . ag {2.41} \end{equation}

Note that $ abla \dg = Hg$. Applying the Schwarz inequality to the last two terms of the right-hand side of (2.41) gives \[ \int _{B_r} \psi ^2 \sum _i abla _{e_i}\dg \wedge * abla _{e_i}\dg + (n-1)H \| \psi \, dg\| ^2_{B_r(x_0)} \] egin{equation} egin{aligned} & \le \| \Delta g\| ^2_{B_r(x_0)} + \left(\| \Delta g\| _{B_r(x_0)} + rac{4}{r^2}\| dg\| ^2_{B_r(x_0)} ight) \ & \quad + \left( rac12\int _{B_r(x_0)} \psi ^2 \sum _i abla _{e_i}\dg \wedge * abla _{e_i}\dg + rac{8}{r^2}\| dg\| ^2_{B_r(x_0)} ight). \end{aligned} ag {2.42} \end{equation}
